questions.q: What does the Calculate Depreciation process do?
options: It retires every asset in a book
It creates new asset categories
It calculates each in-service asset's depreciation for the current period, per book
It transfers journal entries to the General Ledger
questions.explain: Calculate Depreciation runs once per period per book, calculating depreciation for every asset currently in service based on its method, life, and net book value.

questions.q: What is the key difference between preview (draft) mode and final mode?
options: Preview mode is only for tax books
Final mode commits the calculated depreciation and closes the current period; preview mode does not
There is no difference; both close the period
Preview mode can only be run once per year
questions.explain: Preview mode calculates and reports without committing or closing anything, while final mode commits the numbers and advances the book's current open period.

questions.q: When is rollback depreciation the appropriate way to fix a mistake?
options: Any time, even years after the period closed
Only for tax books, never corporate books
Rollback is never appropriate under any circumstances
Immediately after a final run, before accounting has been created against it
questions.explain: Rollback is a narrow window usable before accounting has been created; afterward, a correcting adjustment in a later period is the normal path instead.

questions.q: What happens if assets have failed to depreciate in a given period?
options: The period closes normally and the failures are ignored
Those assets are automatically retired
Depreciation is calculated for them using a default value
The period generally cannot close until the failures are resolved
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion Assets produces an exception report of failed assets, and a period generally cannot close while any assets have failed to depreciate.

questions.q: Why is it standard practice to run preview mode before final mode?
options: Preview mode is required by law in all jurisdictions
Because final mode does not calculate correctly without a prior preview run
Because final mode closes the period, and closed periods generally can't be reopened, so errors should be caught beforehand
Preview mode is only available once per fiscal year
questions.explain: Since final mode closes the period and closed periods generally can't be reopened, reviewing preview results first lets errors be caught and fixed before committing.
